transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 72 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Raman, Marta Kovac (Redwood); Carlos Mendes, Aisha Thompson, Nina Patel, Rory Klein (Evergreen)
---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining — uh we got about 75 minutes today, really appreciative. quick check, audio okay?
[00:08] Carlos: yeah, good here. aisha's on mobile but she's here.
[00:12] Marta: great, i'll take notes. main goal is to walk through IR + BCDR and map to your compliance asks.
[00:18] Priya: perfect. i can drive the technical bits — we'll cover soc2/iso artifacts, sso, audit logs, then deep dive on rto/rpo and escalation.
[00:24] Aisha: sounds good. we primarily care about two things: auditability for regulators and predictable failover for customer-facing flows.
[00:30] Jordan: great, maybe start with a quick run through of your current stack and where Redwood would sit. nina, can you give a 90-second overview?
[00:37] Nina: sure — core is on-prem primary datacenter in eastus, replicated to a warm standby in westus. we run a mix of postgres clusters and a java service layer, but the new ai inference lanes will be in a private cloud tenant, encrypted at rest. currently we do async replication with a few minutes lag — production rpo today is ~5 minutes for ledger but some ancillary services are higher. rto for core banking is 30 minutes target but that assumes db failover automation works. for the initial pilot with Redwood we expect inference to be non-critical but must be PCI scoped for some flows.
[01:12] Priya: good context — so data residency eastus is required for PII and payments; anything with PAN must stay in-region. Redwood Private supports region pinning and KMS integration, we can keep keys under your cloud KMS or use an HSM if needed.
[01:27] Carlos: quick question — if we use Redwood Dedicated versus Private, what's the difference operationally for incident response? who owns runbook steps?
[01:36] Jordan: good one — Dedicated is still Redwood-managed infrastructure but with reserved capacity; we keep control plane in our region. For Private (VPC/private control plane) you get more control: we hand over network access controls and you keep KMS keys. In both cases Redwood supports runbooks and will participate in escalations, but ownership boundaries change: with Private Evergreen owns network and can run tabletop exercises that include their ops team more extensively.
[02:02] Rory: okay, so in private mode we keep KMS custody — is that what you said? that helps legal.
[02:08] Priya: yes, we can integrate with your KMS, support BYOK, and we also produce encryption-at-rest proofs in our reports. plus we can sign audit logs with HSM-backed keys if you need non-repudiation.
[02:20] Aisha: audit logs — retention is important. regulators want seven years for some payment trails. what do you provide and can we export?
[02:28] Marta: we retain detailed API and admin audit logs in our console by default 90 days, but for enterprise/private customers we offer log export to your SIEM and longer retention policies via S3/GCS with lifecycle configs. we can arrange 7-year cold storage exports as part of an enterprise package.
[02:45] Carlos: good to know. and how about tamper evidence?
[02:49] Priya: we support integrity checks and can sign export bundles with KMS keys. there may be some manual steps for on-prem archival but we document the process.
[02:58] [cut — brief crosstalk]
[03:02] Jordan: let's pivot to incident response — what are your typical on-call rotations and the escalation tree? nina?
[03:09] Nina: we have a paged rotation 24/7 for infra; core app owners are on-call business hours. severity classification: sev2 is degraded customer flow, sev1 is outage. we use PagerDuty for notification. currently the SRE runbook includes failover to westus after 2x consecutive failed health checks. question for Redwood: if your model-serving falls over, how does failover work — do you have warm standby or cross-region replication?
[03:36] Priya: Redwood's runtime supports warm-standby across regions for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we have multi-region redundancy but the customer data residency model matters. warm standby means model weights and KV cache primed but not serving until route-switch. replication is asynchronous; we can set up automated cutover with a canary verification step. RTO depends on sequence length and model loading times — typical warm failover for a medium model is 2-6 minutes, cold start can be 12-25 minutes.
[04:05] Aisha: 2-6 minutes is acceptable for non-core flows; but for payment auth path we need sub-60s. could we keep a tiny standby with preloaded light model?
[04:15] Priya: yes — we recommend a small hot-warm configuration for critical low-latency endpoints: keep a compact quantized model replica hot for <1s latency and larger models warm for fallback. this is a cost/latency tradeoff.
[04:27] Carlos: we need numbers for cost modeling.
[04:29] Jordan: we'll send a cost/latency matrix post-call — that's an action.
[04:33] Rory: on legal side, escalation notifications may need to go to our Compliance team within 15 minutes of detection for certain classes. can Redwood push to our webhook or integrate with PagerDuty?
[04:43] Priya: both — we can push events to your webhook, integrate with PagerDuty, and also emit structured audit entries to your SIEM. we have webhooks for incident start/ack/recover. timestamps are synchronized to NTP and included in the payload, though occasional clock skew in log ingestion can exist.
[04:59] Nina: what about RPO for cached KV state? if the model's KV cache is lost on failover, conversation context could be dropped. our UX team flagged that as a risk.
[05:09] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral; for long-running conversations you'd want a session store replicated in your environment. Redwood supports prefix caching and optional session checkpointing to S3 or your DB; that yields an effective RPO equal to your session persistence interval. default is best-effort in-memory cache.
[05:24] [00:05:26 interruption — background noise]
[05:30] Carlos: can we get a written runbook mapping roles? i.e., Redwood escalation to AE > SE > SRE > Eng on-call, and Evergreen triggers.
[05:38] Jordan: yes, we'll supply a runbook showing the joint responsibilities: detection, triage, mitigation, postmortem. it will include contact points and PagerDuty escalation paths.
[05:46] Aisha: SLAs — what's your uptime guarantee for Dedicated/Private? we need 99.95 for prod inference.
[05:52] Marta: Dedicated has SLA options up to 99.95 with credits; Private SLA is negotiated — we typically support 99.9 to 99.99 depending on network ownership and commitments. for private on-prem we provide operational support but SLA is partial because of customer-managed network.
[06:08] Carlos: so if a region outage happens, do you fallback to a different region automatically or is that manual? we need defined sequence to avoid split-brain.
[06:16] Priya: we use smart routing with automated fallback policies. failover can be automatic but we suggest a canary verification (100–200 requests) to confirm model integrity before full cut-over. split-brain risk is mitigated by leader election in the control plane and route quarantines. there are edge cases with sticky session tokens; we'll document those for you.
[06:37] Rory: for compliance we'll need timeline artifacts for any failover event — logs, who executed the cutover, time to recovery, and any data loss assessment. can you provide a downloadable incident packet?
[06:46] Marta: yes, we can produce an incident packet with timeline, logs, audit entries, and root-cause draft. for Dedicated/Private we can retain the related logs beyond the default retention window if requested.
[06:57] Jordan: ok quick run through of the tabletop scenario proposal: we propose simulated eastus region db+model degradation. you (Evergreen) trigger detection, then Redwood coordinates failover to warm-west, execute canary, and return to primary. duration 2 hours including debrief.
[07:12] Nina: that's useful. we want to include the legal/compliance folks for the postmortem for regulator sign-off.
[07:18] Rory: yes please. also want to confirm chain-of-custody for exported logs for evidence.
[07:24] Priya: we can sign logs and provide S3 object manifests; if you require extra proof we can leverage HSM signing.
[07:31] Carlos: last question — any dependency on third-party IDPs for SSO? we use Okta. we need SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning.
[07:38] Priya: Okta is supported, SAML assertions and SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC maps to roles in Redwood Console; for Private we can sync groups and enforce least privilege.
[07:46] Aisha: thanks, helpful.
[07:48] Jordan: recap and actions — we'll send SOC2 + KMS doc, a draft BCDR runbook, and proposed tabletop schedule. any other blockers?
[07:57] Carlos: none from me. nina will collate internal stakeholders and share availability.
[08:01] Rory: send legal checklist please.
[08:03] Marta: will attach our standard evidence checklist and export instructions.
[08:06] Jordan: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up by email with docs and calendar invites.
[08:11] [meeting ends]
